extracted.intended_audience: systematic reviewers, HTA researchers and meta-researchers investigating publication/dissemination bias
extracted.subtask_short: data extraction for publication bias studies
extracted.subtask_description: Templates and guidance for searching, extracting and assessing empirical, methodological and systematic-review evidence about publication and related dissemination biases (search strategies, data items, quality judgements and analytic methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: MEDLINE search strategy (publication bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search terms for MEDLINE focusing on publication/dissemination/language/reporting/grey literature/time delay/citation and related concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Queries shown: *publications/; exp publication bias/; (bias$adj3 (publication$or disseminat$or language$or reporting or grey or gray or citation$or time delay or time lag or national or country or location or conference or abstract or duplicat$or multiple publication$)).tw,ot.; ((reference$or database$or index$) adj2 bias$).tw,ot.; (file adj drawer$).tw,ot.; (time adj2 (completion or publication)).tw,ot.; unpublished research.tw,ot.; (fail$adj2 publish$).tw,ot. Combine with Or/1–8 and limit results to yr='1998–2007'. (Use database-specific field tags as shown.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Cochrane Methodology Register search strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Search terms for Cochrane Methodology Register to identify studies on study identification, unpublished data, updating, small-study effects, funding and outcome reporting bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Queries shown: ‘Study identification’ or ‘Information retrieval’ or ‘Unpublished data’ or ‘Missing data’ or ‘Updating and cumulative meta-analysis’ or ‘Prospective meta-analysis’ or ‘Small study effects’ or ‘Small trial bias’ or ‘Funding’ or ‘Outcome reporting bias’ or ‘Bias in review’ OR (bias* NEAR/3 (publication* or disseminat* or language* or reporting or grey or gray or citation* or time delay or time lag or national or country or location or conference or abstract or reference* or index* or database* or duplicat* or multiple publication*)) in Title, Abstract or Keywords. Limit: from 1998 to 2007 in Cochrane Methodology Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: EMBASE / AMED / CINAHL search strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel search-term sets for EMBASE, AMED and CINAHL targeting publication/dissemination/language/reporting/grey literature/time delay and related biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Queries mirror MEDLINE (bias$adj3 (publication$or disseminat$or language$or reporting or grey or gray or citation$or time delay or time lag or national or country or location or conference or abstract or duplicat$or multiple publication$)).tw,ot. and related adjacency constructs. Combine terms with Or and limit to relevant years (e.g., 1998–2007). Use .tw,ti field tags for AMED/CINAHL as shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEDLINE search strategy – part II (filters)
rubrics_metrics.description: A second MEDLINE strategy combining publication/reporting-bias terms with systematic review/meta-analysis filters and limits on full-text/abstract, date and language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Queries shown: publication bias / reporting bias OR/1–2; systematic review / meta-analysis OR/4–5; combine with AND/7–9; apply filters loattrfull text [sb] AND loattrfree full text [sb] AND has abstract[text]; Date limits 2000 [PDAT]: 2008 [PDAT]; English [lang].

rubrics_metrics.name: Search limits: date and language restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply date and language limits to search results as required (examples shown: yr='1998–2007', 2000–2008, English language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendices repeatedly show applying year limits and language filters; record and report any applied limits when extracting/searching because they affect inclusion and language-bias assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study-identification metadata (empirical studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record standard identification fields: Author (year); Title; Source; Study design & objectives; Reviewer and date (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the top-line fields on the empirical data extraction sheet and must be completed for each study to allow tracking and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes / risk factors and other classification (empirical studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract reported causes/risk factors, existence/identifying information, consequences and other categories relevant to the dissemination bias studied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sheet lists boxes for Causes/risk factors; Existence/identifying; Consequence; Other: ___________. Use these to categorise what the study claims causes or contributes to non-publication or dissemination bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias type taxonomy (empirical & methodological studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify the specific dissemination/publication biases addressed: Publication bias; Language bias; Abstract bias; Database index bias; Duplicate bias; Grey literature bias; Reporting bias; Time delay bias; Citation bias; Media attention bias; Incomplete publication; Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extraction forms provide check-box lists of biases — tick all that apply and use 'Other' to capture additional types. This taxonomy should be used consistently across studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study results coding (empirical studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code main study results as Significant/important bias; Non-significant; Can't tell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details and context in the 'Study results: Details' field. Use these categories to summarise whether the study reports evidence of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original authors' conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the original authors' stated conclusions from the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture verbatim where possible in the 'Original authors’ conclusions' field to preserve the authors' interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence type: indirect vs direct
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify whether each study provides indirect or direct evidence about dissemination bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix instruction: 'For indirect evidence, stop. For studies with direct evidence, continue.' Use this to decide whether to proceed to detailed quality assessment and additional items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific rigorousness (empirical studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess scientific rigorousness with hints: prospective or retrospective design, sample selection bias and other validity threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete free-text comments on rigorousness: consider study design, sampling, measurement of publication outcomes and potential confounders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate sample representativeness with hints: research field, participants, outcomes, interventions, study designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how representative the study population is of the broader literature to judge generalisability of the findings about bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of data analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether data analysis methods are appropriate given objectives, available data and methods of data analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Appropriateness of data analysis' field to record whether analyses support the study's conclusions and note any analytic limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether interpretations are appropriate taking account of limitations of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether authors over-interpret indirect evidence, ignore alternative explanations, or fail to account for biases in their own methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall study quality rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate overall study quality: High (without considerable concern on study validity); Moderate (with some concern on study validity); Low (with considerable concern on study validity); Can't tell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use earlier domain assessments (rigorousness, representativeness, analysis, interpretation) to justify the overall rating and record reasons in 'Any other comments'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data extraction items for methodological studies
rubrics_metrics.description: For methodological studies extract: Author/year; Title; Source; Study design; Study objectives (New method / Established method / Evidence of usefulness/limitations); Methods used (literature search, statistical/modelling, publication process, confirmatory studies, etc.); Study registration; Funnel plot; Updating reviews; Research ethics/policy; Purpose of method; Stage of literature review; Dissemination bias types relevant; Main findings and conclusions; Resources required; Reviewer's commentary (validity, usefulness and limitations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fields are on Appendix 3. Record whether the method is intended to Prevent/Reduce/Detect/Adjust bias and at which stage (before/in/after review) it applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and stage of bias-method applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify the method's stated purpose: Preventing bias; Reducing bias; Detecting bias; Adjusting bias; Other and the stage of literature review where it is applied: Before literature review; In literature review; After literature review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps determine how and when a method can be used operationally in systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data extraction items for systematic reviews of treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract review-level characteristics: Participants; Interventions (and control) – categories (Drug, Surgical, Educational/behavioural, Alternative, Other); Outcomes (primary defined? total no. outcomes); Type of review (Narrative / Meta-analysis) and how many; Designs of included studies (RCTs/CCTs/Other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete fields for how differences between studies were investigated (meta-regression/subgroup/I2/P/Narrative/Statistical/Other) and record reported heterogeneity statistics (I2, P).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search comprehensiveness and inclusion of non-published sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Record sources searched (e.g., MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, Psychlit, Cochrane, handsearch, proceedings, experts/authors, company references), language restrictions, inclusion of non-English studies, grey literature/conference abstracts, and other unpublished studies; indicate whether searched and whether included for main analysis or sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the multi-field structure in Appendix 4 to document for each source whether it was Searched / Included / Used in main analysis or sensitivity analysis. Note language constraints and how non-English studies were handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of missing outcome data and outcome reporting bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether outcome reporting bias was considered; whether there were missing outcome data; and methods used to deal with missing data on outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If missing data exist, extract the methods used (imputation, sensitivity analyses, contacting authors, etc.) and whether outcome reporting bias was explicitly assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods used for dealing with publication bias in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Record and evaluate methods used to detect or adjust for publication bias: Not used; Prospective register; Identify unpublished studies; Fail-safe N; Funnel plot; Egger’s method; Modelling; Rank correlation (Begg method); Large scale trials; Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix 4 lists these options—tick all methods used and extract details/results (e.g., shape of funnel plot, Egger p-value, modelling assumptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue discussion and evidence on publication bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether the issue of publication bias was discussed and whether evidence on publication and related bias was available or not, including details (published versus unpublished trial results; shape of funnel plot or related methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture the review authors' description of publication-bias evidence and any quantitative indicators or sensitivity checks they report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis results and authors' conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify meta-analysis results: Not applicable; Statistically significant (at least one primary outcome); Non-significant (primary outcomes). Classify authors' conclusions: Significant/positive; Non-significant/not important; Unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories to relate the presence or absence of detected publication bias to claimed effectiveness/conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessor's judgement on efforts to minimise publication bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate efforts to minimise publication bias as Sufficient / Partial / Insufficient and provide reasons and comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an overall judgement field in the review extraction form; justify with evidence from the review's search, inclusion of grey literature, registry checks and analytical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of publication bias (review-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the risk of publication bias for the review as High / Moderate / Low and provide reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider completeness of search, presence of unpublished data, heterogeneity patterns, small-study effects, and the authors' own sensitivity analyses when assigning risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are all relevant trials included?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether all relevant trials appear to be included in meta-analyses: Yes / No (how many missing) / Unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When 'No', attempt to quantify the number missing and note impact on conclusions; record methods used to identify unpublished or missing trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details field for publication-bias assessment results
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed extraction of evidence on publication and related bias (e.g. differences between published and unpublished trial results; funnel-plot shape; results of Egger/Begg tests; modelling outputs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix 4 asks for 'If available, details (such as results of published trials versus unpublished trials; or shape of Funnel plot or related methods)'. Enter numerical results, plots description and interpretive comments here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources required to use a methodological method
rubrics_metrics.description: For methodological studies/methods extract resources required to use the method (time, data, statistical expertise, software).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This field helps judge feasibility and generalisability of bias-detection or bias-adjustment methods for routine systematic-review use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer’s commentary for methodological studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a reviewer commentary addressing study validity, scientific rigorousness, method’s usefulness and limitations, and any empirical evidence provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a free-text synthesis to aid interpretation and recommendations for use; include whether empirical validation was provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording sensitivity analyses related to searches and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Document whether sensitivity analyses were performed for inclusion of non-English studies, grey literature, or unpublished studies and the methods used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix 4 contains yes/no boxes and 'If yes, search methods:' fields—capture what was done and how it affected results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables of main characteristics for cohort/regulatory studies
rubrics_metrics.description: For inception cohort studies and regulatory cohort studies extract the main characteristics (cohort source, follow-up, jurisdiction/regulatory authority, outcomes assessed, publication status, dates and sampling frames).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices 5 and 6 provide tabular layouts; populate key fields to enable cross-study comparisons (e.g., proportion published, time-to-publication, selective reporting indicators).
